newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia retenders giant Dukat silver mining plant.
newsitem.headline: Russia retenders giant Dukat silver mining plant.

text.p: Russia opened an investment tender on Tuesday for its financially-troubled Dukat silver mining complex, developer of the former Soviet Union's largest silver mine, by offering a 49 percent stake, Interfax news agency said.
It said that bids for the tender, which replaces an earlier sale that was declared invalid, would be accepted through April 1 with results to be made available April 2.
The tender offers 139.58 million shares at a starting price of 10,000 roubles ($1.76), it said.

Under the terms of the sale, the winner must also transfer to the company at least 20 percent of the $77.7 million needed in initial investment to modernise the plant within one month of signing a formal deal to acquire the shares, Interfax said.
The remainder must be invested by the second half of 1999.
The mining and milling complex is based in the Russian Far East's northeastern Magadan region and contains about two-thirds of Russia's total unmined silver reserves.
The winner must also pay off Dukat's debt within three years. The debt stood at 228 billion roubles as of October 1996.
The Magadan regional property fund declared the previous Dukat investment tender, which required $114 million in investment, invalid for unspecified reasons.

Interfax said that Canada's Pan American Silver Corp, Cyprus Amax Minerals Co of the United States, Arian Resources Corp of Britain and Russia's unknown International Organisation of Information and Investigations, were among those who bid in the annulled tender.
